instructions:
You review whether a regulatory clause has been faithfully turned into a checklist item. Start from the
CLAUSE: work out exactly what it obliges a manufacturer to do (who, what, how often, under which conditions,
how strongly), then judge whether the item captures that and nothing more.

A clause often holds several separate obligations, and each becomes its own item. COVERS shows which part of
the clause this item claims. Work out the complete obligation that part belongs to (a condition, number,
frequency or qualifier attached to it is part of it, even if COVERS cuts it off) and judge the item against
that obligation only. Separate obligations elsewhere in the clause are not the item's job.

Answer every question strictly:
- required_by_clause: is the item's demand actually an obligation stated in this clause (true/false)?
- item_adds: what the item demands beyond the clause (empty string if nothing).
- item_omits: what the covered obligation includes that is missing from the item: any condition, number,
  frequency or qualifier (empty string if nothing).
- strictness: compared with the clause the item is "same", "stricter" or "looser".
- plant_types_ok: does the clause cover every plant type the item is tagged with (true/false)?
- strength_ok: does the item's strength label match the clause's verb (shall/must = mandatory,
  should = recommended, may = optional) (true/false)?
- verdict: "correct" only when the item is faithful on every point above; otherwise "incorrect".
- reason: one or two sentences.

The self- inspection programme should be designed to detect any shortcomings in the implementation of GMP and to recommend the necessary corrective actions. Self-inspections should be performed routinely, and may be, in addition, performed on special occasions, e.g. in the case of product recalls or repeated rejections, or when an inspection by the health authorities is announced. The team responsible for self-inspection should consist of personnel who can evaluate the implementation of GMP objectively. All recommendations for corrective action should be implemented. The procedure for self-inspection should be documented, and there should be an effective follow-up programme. Items for self-inspection

ITEM: Maintain an effective follow-up programme for self-inspections.
Strength: recommended
Plant types: INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
COVERS: there should be an effective follow-up programme

Source: INDIA - Revised Schedule M (G.S.R. 922(E)) Parts I-XIII

Clause Part I 10.4:

Strength: mandatory
Plant types: API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI

Clause 8.9:
8.9 Before suppliers are approved and included in the approved suppliers’ list or specifications, they should be evaluated. The evaluation should take into account a supplier’s history and the nature of the materials to be supplied. If an audit is required, it should determine the supplier’s ability to conform with GMP standards.

ITEM: Evaluate suppliers before approving them and adding them to the approved supplier list or specifications.
Strength: recommended
Plant types: INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
COVERS: Before suppliers are approved and included in the approved suppliers’ list or specifications, they should be evaluated.
